output.brief: Store 14's rising shrink is not yet shown to be a real rise in losses. The figures are interim estimates with an error margin of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across the chain, about half of the stores that showed two consecutive rises (13 of 27) were not confirmed by the year-end count. Store 14's earlier full counts were 1.5–1.8%. The reported rise is 0.8 points over two quarters. The shoplifting log counts rose chain-wide after the new incident app launched on 1 April, so that rise is not specific to store 14. The ethics-line tip was checked on CCTV and the stocker was carrying cardboard bales, so suspending him would be unjustified. The department mix is stable, so a change in what the store sells does not explain the rise. Self-checkout and the bus interchange are both plausible but unproven. The two nearby stores without them were flat or falling, which is only weak, indirect evidence. I'm fairly confident in the next step. Keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject dropping it. Hold off on guards, pulling or staffing the self-checkout lanes, and any personnel action until the count result is compared with the interim figures. Then act on what the count shows. If the rise is confirmed, look at the department and product-class detail.
